flags.reasoning: The prior period text is a standard boilerplate cross-reference to risk factors in the Annual Report and subsequent SEC filings. This is routine forward-looking statement safe-harbor language that commonly appears or disappears between quarterly filings based on editorial placement. There is no substantive regulatory or legal risk disclosure that was removed.

The prior period disclosed specific adjusted operating income of $325 million (15.7% margin) vs. $294 million (14.5%), and a restructuring cost range of $60-$70 million. The current period replaces these with only an adjusted EBITDA margin reference (21.8% vs 20.8%) without the corresponding dollar amounts or restructuring cost guidance. Additionally, the current period added a notable sustainability disclaimer stating that environmental/sustainability plans 'are not an indication that these statements are necessarily material to investors.' However, detailed segment-level operating metrics do appear elsewhere in the filing (as seen in Flag 6 excerpts), so the restructuring guidance may have been moved or simply not repeated in this particular passage.
flags.investigation_action: Verify whether the $60-$70 million restructuring cost guidance for the full year was updated, reiterated, or dropped entirely in the current 10-Q. Check if the new sustainability materiality disclaimer signals a retreat from prior ESG commitments or quantitative targets.

overall.summary: XYL's disclosure quality is generally strong, with exceptionally detailed revenue, segment, and order/backlog reporting. Three of the seven flags were inverted (identifying XYL as the stronger discloser vs. peers). The two legitimate concerns are the thinness of supply chain/tariff risk discussion in MD&A relative to close peers, and the potential removal of specific restructuring cost guidance between quarters. These merit monitoring but do not constitute a pattern of systematic obfuscation.
